- As a result, the data plane doesn't detect any avail, doesn't check `podCache`, doesn't call `decider`, and stitches nothing (playing origin default content / slate).
- Furthermore, even if the session was previously decided for this break before reconnecting, `detectAvails` returning `[]` means it doesn't find the avail, so it never looks up the cached pod in `podCache`!

Wait! How should `detectAvails` handle a manifest that starts *mid-break* (i.e. contains segments inside an ad break leading up to `#EXT-X-CUE-IN`, without a preceding `#EXT-X-CUE-OUT` in the manifest)?
Wait! If a manifest contains `#EXT-X-CUE-IN` and has segments preceding it in the manifest (before any other discontinuity or cue out), are those segments part of an ad break that started before the window?
Wait, what is the start sequence of such an avail? Or how does `opportunityId` get determined?

    for (const avail of avails) {

      const cached = await podCache.get(session, avail.opportunityId);
      if (cached) pod = cached.pod;
